text.content:
Silk Points are the economy of the heist. They represent your spider's preparation, focus, and the specific desperate improvisation that only happens when you're three squares from the prize and the vacuum just switched on.

You start with WIT + NERVE + 1 Silk Points (not counting your species bonus — Silk is practice, not anatomy). When they're gone, they're gone — there's no mid-heist refill. There's only spending well, earning a few back through spectacular failure, and rationing the rest.

CostEffect
1 SP — Extra DieAdd 1 die to a roll before it's made. The most common spend, and a good one. Silk dice don't count toward the +2 bonus-dice limit.
1 SP — Silk LineRun a silk line between two points up to 5 squares apart, for climbing, swinging, or rigging. No roll, but it still takes your Action. (With nothing watching or closing in, a Silk Line needs no roll and no SP. It makes a climb or crossing safe footing; under pressure, it lowers that roll's Difficulty by 1.)
2 SP — RerollAfter rolling, reroll up to 3 dice that didn't succeed. Your Successes stay, so it can only help. For when the dice have wronged you personally.
2 SP — Web StructureBuild a small web structure with no roll — a net, a tripwire, a platform, a hammock. The hammock has no tactical use. The Tinkerer built it anyway.
2 SP — ImproviseSwap the called-for Skill for one of yours that could plausibly work — Engineering to rig a hoist instead of Athletics to climb, Deception instead of Stealth — at +1 Difficulty, rolled with the new Skill's own Attribute. A last resort for working outside your specialty.
3 SP — Silk ClutchAfter a Failure on your own roll (a Partial isn't one, and a Botch die can't be saved), spend 3 SP to turn it into a Success. The Alert rises by 1. You did it, at a cost.
3 SP — Damage ControlThe crew spends 3 SP between them, split any way, to reduce one Alert spike of +2 or more by 1. Once per heist. Call it before the round ends.
4 SP — Not Part of the PlanNegate one complication the ST just introduced, a Partial's included — used immediately, before consequences resolve. Once per heist. The complication doesn't happen. You explain later how you accounted for it. You didn't.

RewardWhen
+1 SP — Flaw MomentYour Flaw causes a genuine problem the crew has to deal with — once each time it fires; no Flaw pays twice.
+1 SP — Spectacular FailureYou fail in a way that genuinely makes the table laugh. ST's call.
+1 SP — Creative Species UseYou use your species ability in a way nobody saw coming, and it works.
+2 SP — Brilliant PlanYou describe a plan that makes the whole table lean in and say “oh, that's good,” and the ST agrees.

Earned Silk can take you above your starting total. Silk is your own: you spend it on your own rolls (your Assist roll included) and on anything you spin. Only Damage Control and Not Part of the Plan take Silk from the whole crew. You can't spend it on a crewmate's roll.

The classic mistake is finishing a heist with Silk still in the pool — you start the next job fresh, so unspent Silk is wasted. Spend it on any roll that matters, from the first obstacle on, and remember that a 1 SP die before a roll is worth more than a 3 SP Silk Clutch after one. Keep 3 back only when the Alert nears its Limit, for the Clutch that saves the objective. A Reroll that only lifts a Failure to a Partial costs you the Clutch (a Partial can't be Clutched) and still costs the Partial's +1 — when the roll matters that much, Clutch instead. Rarely rolling? Put your Silk into your Assists, the crew's lines and webs, Damage Control and Not Part of the Plan.
